---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/fccview/jotty
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: ghcr.io/fccview/jotty:1.26.1
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: none. Jotty is file-based; there is no database to provision.
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0174
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: jotty
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: THE FIRST PERSON TO OPEN /auth/setup, AND THEY GET SUPERADMIN. Verified in app/_server/actions/auth/index.ts:170-174, where the first account created is given isAdmin and isSuperAdmin, and in app/(loggedOutRoutes)/auth/setup/page.tsx:16-19, where the setup page stops serving the form only once a user exists. There is no bootstrap token, no environment variable that pre-creates the account, and no setting that disables the setup page. Upstream provides NOTHING that closes this at deploy time, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying it. So the window is open from the moment the hostname answers until you finish the form, and THE ONLY THING THAT CLOSES IT IS CLAIMING THE ACCOUNT. Do it as the very first thing after the deploy reports healthy, before you hand the URL to anybody, and then run the check in this file, which requires /auth/setup to redirect."
  - "AFTER THAT FIRST ACCOUNT THERE IS NO PUBLIC SIGN-UP AT ALL, which is the good half of the same design. There is no /auth/register route: the only pages under (loggedOutRoutes)/auth are login, setup and verify-mfa, and further users are created by the administrator in the admin panel. Note where the guard actually sits, in case you are tempted to rely on it for anything else: the check is on the setup PAGE, not in the register action, which only rejects a duplicate username."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, from proxy.ts:44-78. Everything except /auth, /public/ and /api/ redirects to the login page without a session cookie, so notes and checklists are not browsable. Two exceptions matter. First, ALL of /api/ bypasses that middleware (proxy.ts:58-60) and each route enforces its own auth with an x-api-key header; GET /api/health is deliberately anonymous and is what the script below uses as its positive control. Second, SERVE_PUBLIC_IMAGES, SERVE_PUBLIC_FILES and SERVE_PUBLIC_VIDEOS each turn a signed-in-only attachment route into an anonymous one (see app/api/file/[username]/[filename]/route.ts:21-22). LEAVE ALL THREE UNSET on a public hostname unless the user asks for public links and understands what they are."
  - "⛔ SET HTTPS TO THE LITERAL STRING true, NOT yes. This one is invisible until something half-works. app/_utils/env-utils.ts:1-18 treats anything that is not no, false or 0 as enabled, so HTTPS=yes gives you a Secure cookie named __Host-session. But server.js:52-55 compares process.env.HTTPS to the exact string \"true\" when it authenticates the WebSocket upgrade, and with HTTPS=yes it looks for a cookie plainly named session, which no longer exists, so every WebSocket connection is rejected 401 while the rest of the app looks fine. Write HTTPS: \"true\". Also keep NODE_ENV production, because the secure-cookie branch requires both."
  - "⛔ SET APP_URL TO THE FULL PUBLIC URL, AND GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF BEFORE YOU DEPLOY. proxy.ts:71-78 builds its login redirect from APP_URL and falls back to whatever origin the request appears to have, which behind a proxy is how you get redirected to the wrong host and never manage to log in. It has to be the exact https URL, so generate the name in full jotty-<8 lowercase alphanumeric>.redu.cloud form up front, pass it to deploy_compose as the dname, and put the same string in APP_URL. Set INTERNAL_API_URL to http://localhost:3000 at the same time: proxy.ts:81-84 uses it for the server-to-itself session check and would otherwise send that call back out through the public proxy on every request."
  - "⛔⛔ FILE OWNERSHIP IS THE THING MOST LIKELY TO BREAK A FIRST ATTEMPT, AND IT FAILS QUIETLY. The image chowns /app/data and /app/.next to 1000:1000 at build time and NEVER creates /app/config (Dockerfile:44-56). docker-entrypoint.sh:15-27 only repairs ownership when PUID or PGID is set to something other than 1000; at the defaults it drops straight to uid 1000 and repairs nothing. So a volume mounted at /app/config comes up owned by root and the app, running as uid 1000, silently cannot write themes, emojis or custom CSS to it. The compose in this file therefore runs a one-shot busybox init service that chowns the three volumes to 1000:1000 before the app starts. That init service is OUR construction, not upstream's; upstream's README instead tells you to chown the directories on the host by hand, which is not something a deploy tool can do for you."
  - "THERE IS NO SECRET ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE HERE, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A GAP. Almost every app in this library has one value that a redeploy destroys: an encryption key, a session secret, an app key. Jotty has none. Sessions are opaque 32-byte random ids written to data/users/sessions.json and looked up there (app/_server/actions/auth/index.ts:50, server.js:26-35), so there is nothing to sign and nothing to lose. What a redeploy destroys instead is THE VOLUME, and the volume is the entire application state. Do not go looking for a SECRET_KEY to set; do make sure the data volume survives."
  - "WHAT THE VOLUMES ACTUALLY HOLD, because two of the three are not obvious. /app/data is EVERYTHING: data/users/users.json (accounts, the password hash and any API key), data/users/sessions.json and session-data.json, data/notes/<user>/ and data/checklists/<user>/ as plain Markdown files, data/sharing/shared-items.json, data/encryption/<user>/ with the PGP key pair, data/logs/ and data/settings.json, plus every uploaded image, file and video under the per-user directories. /app/config is small and optional: custom.css, themes.json, emojis.json and a settings.json override. /app/.next/cache is the Next.js render cache and is genuinely disposable, mounted only so a restart does not start cold. Lose /app/data and you have lost the product; upstream says so in the README in as many words."
  - "PORT 3000 INSIDE THE CONTAINER. Upstream's own compose publishes it on host port 1122, which is a habit from running several apps on one NAS and has no meaning here. Publish 3000 and pass port 3000 to deploy_compose. Health probe: GET /api/health, which answers {\"status\":\"healthy\",\"version\":\"...\"} with no authentication."
  - "PIN THE MULTI-ARCH TAG, NOT AN ARCHITECTURE ONE. ghcr.io/fccview/jotty publishes 1.26.1 alongside 1.26.1-amd64 and 1.26.1-arm64; you want the plain one. 1.26.1 was the newest release on 2026-08-17. Never a rolling tag: upstream's versioning note says a middle-number release may change data structures and run an automatic migration on first launch, which is exactly the thing you do not want a restart to trigger unannounced."
  - "TWO PASSWORD-SHAPED FACTS WORTH ONE SENTENCE EACH TO THE USER. Passwords are stored as an UNSALTED sha256 hash in data/users/users.json (app/_server/actions/auth/index.ts:46-48), so generate a long random one rather than a memorable one. And an API key, when the user generates one in their profile, is the string ck_ followed by 32 hexadecimal characters produced by Math.random rather than a cryptographic source (app/_server/actions/api/index.ts:25-31), and it grants full access to that account and is stored in plaintext beside the hash. Neither is a reason not to deploy it; both are reasons to use a strong password and to only create an API key when something actually needs one. Brute-force protection on the login form is ON by default and locks an account after 3 failed attempts; do not set DISABLE_BRUTEFORCE_PROTECTION."
  - "MFA IS AVAILABLE AND OFF BY DEFAULT. It is a per-user setting under Profile, not an environment variable. On a public hostname it is the single best thing the owner can turn on after claiming the account, so offer it at handover rather than leaving it to be discovered."
  - "SET STOP_CHECK_UPDATES=yes IF THE USER WANTS NO OUTBOUND CALLS. Left unset, the app calls the GitHub API to tell you when a new version exists. Harmless, and some people want to know before it happens."
  - "NO DATABASE, SO DO NOT PROVISION ONE. This is worth saying out loud because the reflex on this platform is to add a managed Postgres. Jotty stores everything as Markdown and JSON files on disk; there is no database adapter, no connection string and nothing for redu's PGHOST or DATABASE_URL to attach to. Passing database:'managed' would create a second VM that bills and that nothing ever connects to."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. The README and the whole howto directory give no RAM or disk number. m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB / 20 GB) is reasoning from a prebuilt Next.js standalone server on node:20-alpine with no database process and no build step. The constraint to watch is DISK, not memory: notes and checklists are tiny Markdown files, but image, file and video uploads land in the same volume and the request body limit defaults to 100mb, so anyone planning to paste video into notes should start on m1.medium for its 40 GB. Growing it later is a volume resize, not a redeploy, so put that in front of the user BEFORE they approve the plan."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> generate the dname -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.017/hr, roughly GBP 13 a month, the cheapest kind of entry there is because there is no database VM; inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), NO database, port 3000. plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large; pass flavor_id explicitly and hold m1.small, since nothing here is built from source."

  - "LICENCE: GNU AGPL v3, read from the LICENSE file. AGPL section 13 puts an obligation on whoever OPERATES the service: if you modify Jotty and let other people use it over a network, those users must be offered the modified source. Running the unmodified official image for yourself or your household triggers nothing extra. One sentence at handover; not a legal opinion."

That also means there is no copy of the notes anywhere else. Say that plainly before deleting, and point the user at the export feature or a copy of the data volume first."

# Self-host Jotty on redu

Notes and checklists as plain Markdown files on a machine you own, with a public HTTPS URL and no
database to run. About GBP 13 a month, which is as cheap as this library gets.

## What this deploys

- **Jotty** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 3000.
- **No database.** Everything is Markdown and JSON on a volume. There is nothing else to provision.
- Three volumes: your data, your customisations, and a disposable render cache.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.017/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Jotty on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Claim the admin account first. Everything else can wait.

The first person to open `/auth/setup` creates the account, and that account is both admin and
superadmin. Upstream ships no bootstrap token, no environment variable that pre-creates it, and no
setting that turns the setup page off, so there is nothing to configure here: the window is open
from the moment the hostname answers until somebody fills in the form.

So claim it as part of the deploy, before the URL is handed to anyone, and then prove the window
is shut with the script below.

## The compose file

Two services. The second exists only because the image never creates `/app/config` and drops to
uid 1000 without repairing ownership, so a fresh volume mounted there would be unwritable.

```yaml
services:
  init-perms:

# Self-host Jotty on redu

Notes and checklists as plain Markdown files on a machine you own, with a public HTTPS URL and no
database to run. About GBP 13 a month, which is as cheap as this library gets.

## What this deploys

- **Jotty** from the official image, pinned, on one m1.small VM, port 3000.
- **No database.** Everything is Markdown and JSON on a volume. There is nothing else to provision.
- Three volumes: your data, your customisations, and a disposable render cache.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.017/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

setting that turns the setup page off, so there is nothing to configure here: the window is open
